object_description: two buildings facing each other across the stream forming a built front, one partially buried
design_condition: the organisation is built around the bed of the existing stream, with two buildings facing each other across it forming a front to the south-west and clearing a large outdoor space to the north-east

positive: The organisation is built around the bed of the existing stream
Two buildings facing each other form a built front to the south-west
A large space is cleared to the north-east for all the exterior fittings
The major outdoor space gathers the access and covered courtyard functions of the buildings
Pedestrian flows connect to the village from the south while vehicles connect to the road in the north
The public building is partially buried, giving a significant amount of natural light in the sports halls
The plan is intended to be economical and compact
The day centre programme benefits from beautiful views of the landscape
The jury recognises the simplicity and rationality of the proposed intervention
The project integrates smoothly into the general topography of the land
It proposes landscaping of the stream and its surroundings
The volume of the triple hall is assumed in the composition with a semi-buried proposal
The open space to the north-east is generously open to the large landscape and connects all access
negative: The equipment rooms are not directly adjoining the sports halls, so routing equipment is impossible
Spreading the day centre over two levels increases traffic and makes supervision of children difficult
The primary rooms are very compact with little clearance space
The rigour and concentration of the class levels did not convince the jury
A weakness in the plan is perceived in terms of educational aspects
The teacher room faces north towards the parking and loses contact with the schoolyard
The immediate proximity of the north-west facade to vehicles seems poorly controlled
Access to the underground car park risks conflict with a potential pedestrian flow
The economic feasibility of an underground car park in this sparsely urbanised context is questioned
The entire building gives off a strong impression of massiveness
The differences between the two volumes leave the panel perplexed
The significant length of the south facade offers a relatively harsh face on the village side
